Bobine

A video editor in which an agent plans, cuts, reviews and corrects an edit according to one of fifteen formats, while rendering runs entirely in the browser so that source footage never leaves the device.

Visit the site ↗How to useEngineering record

Engineering recordFor technical reviewers

Designed and shipped a browser video editor with AI editing agents: on-device decoding and rendering, a serverless AI layer, credit accounting and payments. The main constraint was editing real footage without uploading it.

The user drops clips; the browser decodes them, extracts up to 24 keyframes per clip at 512 px and 16 kHz mono audio, and sends only those. Each function validates its input with zod, reserves credits through a database function, calls the model through the gateway with fallbacks and a deadline, and refunds the reservation if the call fails. The returned notes and word timings drive cuts aligned to the music, and the final render happens on the device.

Key engineering decisions

01

Render on the device

Video stays local and the server never handles large files, which removes upload time, storage cost and most privacy exposure. The trade-off is that capability depends on the browser’s WebCodecs support.

02

Charge before, refund on failure

Credits are spent by a database function before the model call and refunded by reference afterwards if it fails, so a user is never charged for an error and cannot overspend with parallel requests.

03

Bill on server-read duration

Transcription is billed from the WAV header the server reads, never from a duration the client claims.

Notes for reviewers

Limits and next stepsOnly one end-to-end test file exists; the next step is contract tests for each function and a browser test of a full edit and export.
01

Problem statement

Creators who publish every day spend their evenings editing on a telephone. Consumer applications give amateur results, professional software takes months to learn, and cloud editors require uploading gigabytes over metered mobile data.

02

Contribution

The user selects a format and adds footage and music; a format-specific agent drafts a plan, performs the cut, reviews it and applies corrections. Captions, titles, colour and music levels are set automatically, and revisions are requested in plain language. Cinéma generates AI scenes from a specified camera position, movement and lighting.

03

Architecture

A React application whose rendering runs in the browser through the WebCodecs API. Application data are kept in Postgres, model calls pass through an AI gateway, and payments use Stripe.

04

Method and data

The source files never leave the device: the model receives at most 24 keyframes per clip, downscaled to 512 pixels, and mono 16 kHz audio in chunks of up to 60 seconds for transcription, and returns notes and timings that drive the edit. Cut points are aligned with the beats of the music track. Credits are reserved before each model call and refunded automatically when the call fails.

05

Verification and limitations

Because rendering depends on WebCodecs, capability varies with the browser and the device. The thirteen demonstration edits in the gallery were made from licensed stock footage.
